# The project

## Where do the data come from? (To which population will results generalize?)

The dataset consists of a large collection of tweets and comments posted on other platforms
that may contain hurtful or otherwise derogatory messages.

The dataset was merged and standardized through a series of preprocessing steps applied to the raw text:

1. Normalization: extra spaces, hyperlinks, user mentions, emojis/emoticons (converted to text), and newline characters were removed.
2. Text expansion and correction: contractions were expanded (e.g., isn't → is not, lmao → laughing my ass off). Grammatical corrections were made by comparing candidate sentences using word mover’s distance, leveraging Google News Word2Vec embeddings (Word2Vec) and the open-source Gensim implementation (Gensim Word2Vec).
3. Dates and times were removed.
4. Accented characters and numbers (e.g., êá, 12) were removed.
5. Remaining numeric values were converted to words.
6. Ampersands at the beginning of words were removed.
7. A predefined set of special characters (_"-;%()|+&=*%.,!?:#$@[]/) was stripped from the text.
8. Misspelled profanities were corrected to their standard forms using a publicly available lexicon of English profanity.
9. All lower case.

Following these steps, the resulting dataset was class-balanced by downsampling the majority class to achieve an approximate 1:1 ratio between classes.
Real content is less than 50% offensive (I hope), so accuracy and predicted probabilities won't translate to the real world.
